exam: What is the first step in a patient with suspected TLS? — Aggressive IV hydration to achieve urine output ≥80 mL/h and baseline labs.
Which drug is contraindicated in a patient with severe hyperkalaemia? — Furosemide if volume depleted, as it can worsen potassium loss.
How would you differentiate tumour lysis from haemolysis on labs? — Look for schistocytes and elevated LDH; tumour lysis shows rising uric acid and phosphate.
What is the most appropriate prophylaxis for a high‑risk lymphoma patient? — Allopurinol started before chemotherapy, with aggressive hydration.
When is dialysis indicated in TLS? — Refractory hyperkalaemia >6.5 mmol/L, severe acidosis, or oliguria despite fluids.
Why is calcium not given in early TLS? — Hypocalcaemia is secondary to hyperphosphataemia; giving calcium can precipitate calcium‑phosphate stones.
ai.title: Tumour Lysis Syndrome
ai.subject: Medicine
ai.summary: A rapid release of intracellular contents after tumour cell death causes electrolyte shifts and renal failure. Early recognition and aggressive hydration plus uric‑acid control are lifesaving.

b: Occurs after chemotherapy, radiotherapy or spontaneous tumour lysis.
Common in high‑grade lymphomas, leukaemias and solid tumours with high proliferation.
